paraphrase: The marks of the wise (paṇḍita): he practises what is praiseworthy and avoids what is blamed, has faith and is not a denier; anger, joy, pride, shame, obstinacy and vanity do not draw him from his purpose; others know his deeds only when done; cold and heat, fear and love, prosperity and adversity do not obstruct his work.
speaker: Vidura

paraphrase: Dharma alone is the highest good, forgiveness alone the highest peace, knowledge alone the highest vision, non-violence alone brings happiness.

paraphrase: Relatives, friends and sons turn back and leave a man cast into the fire; only the deed he himself has done follows him.

paraphrase: The self is a river with sacred fords, Bhārata, its water truth, its banks steadfastness, its waves self-restraint; one of good deeds who bathes in it is purified — the self is ever pure, not water.
The śūdra who serves the brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya and vaiśya duly in order, when they are satisfied, is freed of sin, and leaving the body enjoys the happiness of heaven.
